summary: Read Mond–Portier 2201.11805 in full: Lemma 2.3's proof bounds every dyadic scale of aum uniformly (eq. (5)) and never restricts m to polylog size; the paper's own step gives aum ≤ 4x. Exact A3(p) for all primes p ≤ 30000 (script SK0_a3.c): the share of representable m with m ≤ (log2 p)^3 falls from 0.98 (p<10^3) to 0.79 (p in [2·10^4,3·10^4)), while the share with m ≤ √p rises 0.21→0.28; the largest m is 2p+1 in every case (trivial rep 1+1+1/p). So polylog support is neither proved nor supported by the data at this scale.
not_done: Only p ≤ 3·10^4 and only C=3 tested; no attempt at a proof of support.
next: Run the C counter to p=10^6 and measure the tail share above (log2 p)^C for C=3,4,5 to see whether it vanishes.

summary: In Z[√2] the cone |x|,|x'| ≥ 1 is symmetric under x→−x, so rational denominators are arbitrary nonzero integers and the cone is signed-integer ES. For every n not a power of 3, x=n, y=ns, z=ns/e with e=±q (q a prime factor ≠3, sign chosen so e≡2 mod 3), s=(e+1)/3 gives 4/n exactly; verified for 2≤n≤10^4 (7832 of these are fully positive). So the norm-bound cone collapses to a trivial problem on rational targets.
not_done: Irrational denominators in Z[√2] (the actual hard twin) were not searched.
next: Replace the cone by one that is positive on all embeddings and closed under multiplication (a real order), then test.

summary: Epstein (arXiv:2305.16518, Main Theorem 2.10): a Euclidean D is Egyptian (R(D)=K) or R(D) is a DVR whose units+0 form a field; Z, Z[i], Z[√2] are Egyptian (Cor. 2.13). For F_q[T], R ⊆ O_∞ (every 1/f has degree ≤ 0) and R ≠ K, so by the DVR property R = O_∞: sums of unit fractions never reach rational functions of positive degree at ∞, at any length. ES targets 4/f never hit it, so there is no obstruction for ES.
not_done: Did not check the function-field DVR identification beyond the containment argument.
next: None for ES; if pursued, study the O_∞ obstruction for non-ES targets.

summary: Checked the Egyptian-domain papers: Z is Egyptian (GLO22), and in Epstein's Egyptian-domain paper (arXiv:2303.15685) the full text contains no bound on the number of terms (grep for 'terms', 'length', 'bounded' gives no relevant hit); Egyptian means R=K, i.e. unbounded length. There is therefore no length-bounded ES statement to extract; the repo 'covered' only cited the analogue index.
not_done: Did not read the GLO22 PDF (not on arXiv).

summary: Repo Prop 3.3 (BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md) gives positive ES over O_K for every n≥2 when K is real quadratic with N(ε)=−1. In the Weil restriction (6 integer coordinates, 2 rational equations) the slice b=0 is exactly the ES equation over Z (3 unknowns, 1 equation), so 'curves through the Prop 3.3 points meeting b=0' asks whether an irrational solution family connects to a rational one. I formalised this but did not run a curve search; no finite test was defined.
not_done: Curve search through Prop 3.3 points not executed.
next: Take n=5 and n=9 Prop-3.3 solutions, look for rational lines/conics in the 6-space through them, and test whether they meet b=0 at integer points.

summary: Computed for all 429 primes p≤3000 (exact rep search; an exact rep exists for every one, so the best 3-term underapproximation has gap 0): the greedy first term g1=⌊p/4⌋+1 extends to an exact 3-term rep for 401/429 primes; the smallest first denominator of an exact rep is within ⌈p/4⌉+5 for every prime (offsets 0:401, 1:24, 2:1, 3:1, 5:2). Pass 1 cited the Kovač/Nathanson papers, which are abstracts only, and did no computation.
not_done: Did not compute the best 3-term underapproximation explicitly for p>3000 (the gap-0 equivalence is used); p≤10^4 not run.
next: Extend to p≤10^4 (KMAX larger) and record the offset distribution.

summary: Read the full Elsholtz–Planitzer paper (arXiv:2012.05984): the k=4 results (eqs. (5),(7)) are upper bounds on the count f_4(m,n) only; no pointwise existence statement for 4-term representations of m/n is proved or cited there. The Elsholtz–Tao k=3 bound is the only pointwise-type input.
not_done: Did not survey other literature for 4-term existence.

summary: Mustață's notes (impan.pl/~pragacz/mustata1.pdf, §1) state that for f = x_1^{a_1}+…+x_n^{a_n}, lct_0(f) = min(1, Σ 1/a_i). So the lct values of 3-variable Brieskorn–Pham sums are exactly min(1, 1/a+1/b+1/c), and '4/n = lct' is the ES equation restated; no new content.
evidence: Mustață lecture notes (impan.pl/~pragacz/mustata1.pdf), Ex. around l.52

summary: Formalised: an n×4 rectangle tiled by three horizontal strips of equal squares forces 4/n = Σ_{i=1}^3 1/x_i by area comparison. Two-level strip refinements yield sums with more terms, so they give no constraint beyond the equation; no Dehn-type literature check was done.
not_done: No literature check on rectangle tilings.

summary: Read Elsholtz–Heuberger–Prodinger (arXiv:1108.5964, Def. 1): their 'unit fractions' are powers t^{-x_i} with Σ t^{-x_i}=1 (Kraft equality). So the memo's claim that 3-leaf subtrees encode ES fails: the denominators are powers of t, and 4/n with odd n (or with a prime factor ≠ t) cannot be a sum of three such terms.

Enumerated all 14 multisets a1≤…≤a4 with Σ1/a_i=1 (max denominator 42, e.g. 1=1/2+1/3+1/7+1/42). Class-equation multisets for groups with 4 conjugacy classes (C4, C2², D10, A4, from the recalled small-group list) realise only three of them: (4,4,4,4), (2,5,5,10), (3,3,4,12). The other eleven are not realised by these groups; no ES content.
not_done: The 4-class group list is recalled, not verified against a database.

summary: Gauss–Bonnet: a triangle with angles π/x, π/y, π/z (x,y,z from an ES triple) has area π(1−4/n) = π(n−4)/n, the defect the item quotes; the triangle group Δ(x,y,z) exists for every such triple, so the tiling reading is the ES equation again. No new test.
not_done: No computation of Wythoff tilings.

summary: Recorded the hypermap identity N(1/x+1/y+1/z−1)=χ. For an ES triple it becomes N(4−n)/n = χ, so the only requirement is n | N(n−4) (integrality of the dart count N), which N=n satisfies. No obstruction.
not_done: No hypermap enumeration.

summary: Weighted projective planes P(a,b,c) are always Fano (−K = O(a+b+c) is ample), so the well-formedness/Fano conditions impose no constraint on the weights; Σ1/w=4/n is the bare ES equation.

Computed all series–parallel resistances from k unit resistors for k≤6 (distinct values 2,4,9,22,53). The resistance n/4 (= conductance 4/n) appears with k ≤ 6 for many n, e.g. n=12 with 3 units and n=8 with 2, while the minimal 3-branch chain network for ES needs x+y+z units (17 to 329 in range). So the 3-branch chain form is far from minimal in units, and the SP count gives no ES constraint.
not_done: Only k≤6 and n≤30.

summary: Identity check: the minimum of independent exponentials with rates 1/x_i has mean 1/Σ(1/x_i); for ES this is n/4. A reformulation, no test.
Checked algebra: the plane X/x+Y/y+Z/z=1 passes through (t,t,t) iff t(1/x+1/y+1/z)=1, i.e. with t=n/4 it is the ES equation. Pure restatement of the equation in the lattice language.
not_done: No lattice-point computation.

summary: Category check: ES is ∀n ∃(x,y,z) with a decidable matrix, hence a Π2 sentence; the set of n with a witness is c.e. Rationals are computable, so there is no computable-real obstruction. The catalogue's 'Π1' remark is a different logical form.
Category check: Q_p admits no field ordering (it is non-real; −1 is a sum of squares), so 'positivity via an embedding into R' is not defined on Z_p. Standard fact, not re-verified by reference.

Premise check: the item's example {n ≡ 1 mod 4} IS multiplicatively closed (verified on a sample; (1 mod 4)(1 mod 4) ≡ 1 mod 4), so as written it is not a counterexample; the stated cone is also incomplete ('or …'). Recorded as a false premise.

Found Boyd (Experimental Math. 3 (1994), 287–302; projecteuclid 1048515811) on p-adic valuations of partial harmonic sums with a probabilistic model; no ES question enters. The tree technique was not reproduced.
not_done: Boyd's tree technique not reproduced.

summary: Read Ambro–Barcău (arXiv:1412.3263, Thm 0.2(b)); the PDF formula is garbled, and the reading u_{⌊δ⌋+1,q}/(q(1−{δ})) is the one that gives equality for k=1. For 4/p (k=3, δ=3−4/p, q=p) this gives lcm(x,y,z) ≤ p(p+1)(p²+p+1)/4. Checked on all reps of 4/p for primes p≤200: no violation, but the bound is loose (best rep lcm/bound ≤ 0.15). The paper's equality cases do not include 4/p, so no sharpness.
not_done: Formula reading from the PDF text; not checked against the published version.

summary: Exact A3(p) = #{m ≤ 3p, gcd(m,p)=1 : m/p is a 3-term unit-fraction sum} for all primes p≤30000 (C code, cross-checked against brute force for p≤53). Σ_{p≤x}A3(p)/(x log2^3 x) ≈ 0.0122 at x=10^4 and 0.0116 at x≈3·10^4, consistent with the Luca–Pappalardi/Mond–Portier scale x(log x)^3; A3(p)/√p ≈ 3 at p≈3·10^4, consistent with the n^{1/2+o(1)} bound of arXiv:2210.07921.
not_done: Only p ≤ 3·10^4; no fit of log-power exponent.

summary: Among the representable numerators m (exact A3(p), primes p≤30000), the share with 4 | m is 0.226 in every p-range (0.225–0.227), versus 0.25 for uniform m coprime to p. The mod-8 shares are 0.112 (class 0), 0.114 (class 4), 0.125 (1), 0.115 (2), 0.138 (3), so numerators ≡0 mod 4 are depleted by about 10% and the depletion is stable in p. Mond–Portier's method counts all m uniformly and gives no class-restricted lower bound, so this positive-proportion behaviour is not proved.
not_done: Parity explanation via the Type I/II parametrisation not derived; mod-8 classes 5–7 not printed separately.
next: Derive the residue distribution of m mod 4 from the Type I/II formulas and test whether the 0.226 share is forced.

summary: The step needs a map from a totally positive cyclotomic unit η ≡ −1 (mod inert prime) to an ES solution; the item gives none, and none of the natural candidates I considered produces denominators. Not executable as written; I did not invent a map.
not_done: Whole step (no map).
next: Define the map first (e.g. from a trace identity) and then test p=5,13,17.

summary: Premise false: for odd p, 4/n = 1/(n/2) + 1/n + 1/n, with n/2 ∈ Z_(p) because 2 is a unit there, so ES over Z_(p) is trivially solvable for every n. Denominators in Z_(p) need not be integers, so the item's 'trivially equivalent to ES over Z' is wrong. Verified for n<300.
Collapse: if x,y ∈ N then 1/α = 4/p − 1/x − 1/y ∈ Q, and α an algebraic integer in Q means α ∈ Z. So the 'one algebraic denominator' problem is ES over Z with z=α.
Checked: Z[i]^× = {±1, ±i} is finite (order 4), so there are no infinite-order units and the premise holds. Nothing further.
Category check: the group-law sum of points on an elliptic curve is not an ES operation; the item records this itself. No test.

Tropical limit: setting 1/x_i = exp(−u_i/h), the h→0 limit of the sum is min over i of exp(−u_i/h), so the dequantized ES reduces to a min-plus statement that is trivially solvable. No ES content survives the limit.
not_done: No definition of ES_h beyond this limit.

summary: Quaternion search not implemented. I did the commutative case over Z[i] instead: a general search over x,y in a box (|Re|,|Im| ≤ 6, primes ≤200) found signed/complex solutions only (no positivity); the conjugate-pair ansatz x=a+bi, y=a−bi, z∈Z gives 4/p as 2a/(a²+b²)+1/z and was solvable for 42 of 45 primes ≤200 with z≤300, a≤3000. Without a positivity constraint the Gaussian version is trivial, so it says nothing about the commuting-denominator question for ES.
not_done: Hurwitz quaternions and Q(√−d), d≠1 not searched; positivity not imposed.
next: Impose Re>0 or a real-order cone and redo the conjugate-pair search over Z[√−d].

summary: Category check: Q_p has no ordering compatible with multiplication, and the absolute-value 'cone' {|x|_p ≥ c} is not closed under addition; no ES cone results.
Catalogue entry with first step 'None'; no ES-specific question to test in the record, and the repo has no depth document for it.
not_done: No Waring-type ES question was formulated.

summary: Identity 6x = (x+1)^3 + (x−1)^3 − 2x^3 verified algebraically ((x+1)^3+(x−1)^3 = 2x^3+6x). Catalogue identity with no ES content.
Catalogue entry (Catalan / Mihăilescu). Known theorem with no ES content; not re-verified by reference.

Literature (search: MO 510833 'Quantitative side of Pillai's conjecture'): Pillai's conjecture, that x^a−y^b=k has finitely many solutions for each k with x,y,a,b≥2, is open. The ES identity 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) is a three-variable symmetric equation, not of Pillai form, so the conjecture has no bearing on ES representability.
Exact check of n!+1 = m² for 2≤n≤1000 (Python big integers): solutions only n=4,5,7. Brocard's problem is open beyond n=7 (Wikipedia; arXiv:2004.09256 survey). Not an ES quantity.

Verified the two-unit-fraction criterion in the repo's Stewart form on all 8771 coprime pairs m,n≤120 (exhaustive search for x ≤ 2mn): m/n = 1/x+1/y is solvable iff there are coprime divisors d1,d2 of n with m | d1+d2 (0 mismatches). This turns the 2-term step into a divisor check, but the item's auxiliary-N / T1-at-squares reformulation was not tested.
not_done: The subgroup-forcing claim at squares (T1) not tested.

summary: Niederreiter's partial-quotient results concern continued fractions of a/2^k, a/3^k, a/5^k; no ES construction follows from the folding lemma in the record. No computation.
not_done: Folding-lemma construction not attempted.

summary: Shkredov (arXiv:2603.14116, 2026) proves that all partial quotients of a/q are O(√log q), improving the Korobov–Larcher bounds (search result). Partial quotients of a/q are continued-fraction data, not Egyptian-fraction denominators, so the result does not bear on ES.
Duffin–Schaeffer proved (Koukoulopoulos–Maynard, arXiv:1907.04593): full measure for ∑ψ(q)φ(q)/q=∞. No ES relevance.

Dasgupta–Voight (arXiv:1707.05874) prove unconditionally that for prime p≡4,7 mod 9 with 3 not a cube mod p, both x^3+y^3=p and x^3+y^3=p² are solvable; the abstract does not cover p≡8 mod 9 or the remaining 3-cube-residue cases. No ES content.
not_done: Full hypotheses of the Sylvester statement for p≡8 mod 9 not checked.

summary: Gauss class number one (Heegner–Baker–Stark) is a theorem; catalogue entry with no ES content.

Exact check of x²+7 = 2^n for 1≤n≤300: solutions (n,x) = (3,1),(4,3),(5,5),(7,11),(15,181), i.e. the five Ramanujan–Nagell solutions. Nothing ES-related: the equation has two unknowns and no n-parameter of ES type.

Thue's theorem (finitely many solutions of F(x,y)=m for irreducible F of degree ≥3) and Stewart's effective bounds on the number of solutions (J. AMS 4, 1991; search result) were located. ES is a three-variable equation 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx) with parameter n, not a two-variable Thue form, so no bound transfers.
Primitive divisors of elliptic divisibility sequences: uniform estimates exist (Ingram–Silverman); the repo entry (#84) is a height mechanism, not an ES test.

Literature (Wikipedia 'Wieferich prime'; MO 435208): whether there are infinitely many Wieferich primes, and infinitely many non-Wieferich primes, is open; Silverman proved infinitely many non-Wieferich primes for each base. ES involves no p-adic power condition, so nothing transfers.

Literature (Wikipedia 'Hilbert's tenth problem'; arXiv:2510.18794 on undecidability over Z[i]): Hilbert's tenth problem is negative over Z, and the analogous question over Z[i] is undecidable. The ES Π2 form (Z0205) gives no decision procedure, and since ES is one fixed family, the general undecidability does not decide it.
Collatz: Tao (arXiv:1909.03562) gives almost-all almost-bounded results under log density; no pointwise statement; no ES content.
Lagarias' 3x+1 survey (williams.edu PDF, search result) lists the 5x+1 divergent-trajectory conjecture as open and records the known nontrivial cycles. No ES quantity enters the 5x+1 map.
Erdős ternary conjecture on 2^n in base 3: open; partial digit-pattern results only; no ES content.
Odd covering problem: open; Hough (Ann. Math. 2015) solves the minimum-modulus problem, not the odd-covering question. No ES content.
Exact count: 54110 integers n ≤ 10^6 have n²+1 prime (sympy isprime). Landau's problem (infinitely many such primes) is open (search results). The count is a data point only and gives no ES test.

Computed M(x)=Σμ(n) by sieve: max |M(x)|/√x over 2≤x≤10^7 is 0.894 (at x=5), M(10^7)=1037, so no violation in range. Odlyzko–te Riele (J. reine angew. Math. 357, 1985) disproved the conjecture by LLL-based search (search results), so the range check is consistent but not decisive; no ES content.
Perfect cuboid: open; arXiv:2312.09091 is a non-refereed set of conjectures with no proof. No ES content.

Literature (Wikipedia 'abc conjecture'; r/math 2025 thread, search results): Mochizuki's 2012 IUT proof is not accepted by the mainstream, so abc remains unproven in the accepted sense. abc does not decide ES; no computation.
Erdős–Moser: arXiv:0907.1356 gives m > 10^{10^9} for any solution; open in general. No ES content.

Exhaustive check: of the 24 permutations of length 4, exactly 4 avoid a monotone subsequence of length 3; of the 120 of length 5, none do, matching the Erdős–Szekeres bound (r−1)(s−1)+1 = 5 for r=s=3. Monotone subsequences do not relate to unit-fraction representations, so no ES content.
Goldbach for Gaussian/Hurwitz/Eisenstein primes: arXiv:1606.05958 (positive-coefficient sums) and arXiv:2309.14249 (sector versions, almost-all) — no pointwise statement for ES.

Exact check: the largest subgroup of (Z/4C)^× avoiding −1 has index 2 for every C (via the mod-4 character χ with χ(−1)=−1, and −1 is not a square mod 4). Brute force over cyclic witnesses confirmed max density exactly 1/2 for C≤200. Pass 1 cited the dividing memo's Selberg–Delange entries, which do not compute this.
not_done: Only C≤200 brute force; the argument is general.

summary: N_C is not defined in this record (it is the Z0558 'confined count' object, which is not formalised here), so the Bertrand-style size comparison cannot be run as stated; I did not supply a definition.
not_done: Whole step (undefined objects).

summary: Pomerance–Weingartner (arXiv:2007.11062) prove essentially all large odd n are prime + practical number. Practical numbers are not ES certificates; no ES reformulation tested.
Second Hardy–Littlewood: unconditional and RH-conditional ranges (arXiv:2503.02766). No ES content.

Computed #{2≤x≤10^7 : π(x) ≥ li(x)} = 0 by sieve and Ei(ln x) (scipy), with sample values e.g. π(10^7)=664579 < li(10^7)=664918. Littlewood (1914) gives infinitely many sign changes, and the first one (Skewes-type) lies beyond 10^7 (search: Skewes's number; Chao 2010). No ES content.

Chebotarev restatement: Type I at (a,d) is a congruence condition on p mod 4ad (abelian field Q(ζ_{4ad})), so the Galois language adds no prediction beyond the residue-class densities already used in the dividing residue model (scripts/z52b_dividing_avoid.py). Not computed.
not_done: No Galois-group computation.

summary: Hilbert irreducibility (Serre thin sets): classical; the ES relevance is the thin-set transfer already noted, not a new test.
F5 = 2^32+1 = 641·6700417 verified exactly; OEIS A019434 (search result) lists F0–F4 as the only known Fermat primes. Finiteness of Fermat primes is open (heuristic only). No ES content.
Hua's theorem: n = p1²+…+p5² for large n. The arXiv:2402.03076 result is a different statement (one prime square + seventeen fifth powers). No ES content.

Literature (search): Goldston (1990) proves almost all even numbers are Goldbach numbers; short-interval Goldbach–Linnik results (Kim 2024, Chirre 2026) are almost-all statements under zero-free-region hypotheses. No pointwise ES consequence.
AKS: deterministic polynomial primality; the certificate-step question is not an ES test. No ES content.

Literature (Wikipedia 'Erdős–Woods number'; planetmath): Erdős–Woods numbers are characterised by partitions of the primes and there are infinitely many; the search lists 22, 34, 36, 46, 56, … as examples. No ES-side statement is involved.

Exact check of Σ_{k=1}^{n−1} k^{n−1} ≡ −1 (mod n) for 2≤n≤2000: it holds exactly for the primes in that range and for no composite (the Giuga/Agoh-type criterion; Kellner 2004 gives the Giuga–Agoh equivalence, search result). No ES content.

Literature (Wikipedia 'Wiles's proof'; Wiles, Annals 1995, search results): Wiles with Taylor–Wiles proves modularity of semistable elliptic curves, which gives Fermat's Last Theorem. ES has no link to x^n+y^n=z^n, so nothing transfers.
Vague item (count of 'independent parameters vs constraints'); no computable quantity named; ES has 3 unknowns and one equation, nothing more was extracted.
not_done: No quantitative version formulated.

summary: Ramanujan's form x²+y²+10z² (finitely many exceptions under GRH) vs genus-proved x²+y²+z²; literature only, no ES content.
Positivity-region volume: the positive reals have infinite Haar/log measure, so the proposed comparison with R(p) is undefined as stated.

Built the feature matrix from data/z52b/dividing.jsonl (165 items with exactly one outcome tag, 8 tags used ≥5 times) and fitted a depth-3 tree: 5-fold CV accuracy 0.255 versus majority baseline 0.224. The tags barely predict the recorded outcome; the splits are on count:zero and obst:covering.

For m=4 and p>10^18 this is exp(−(41.4)^3/4) ≈ e^{−1.8·10^4} under the unit constant, and Table 1 shows exceptions for m=8..15 only up to n ≈ 2·10^4. A fitted constant κ would need κ ≲ 10^{-3} to give non-negligible mass beyond 10^18; κ was not fitted.

summary: Chunked run of the repo's residue model with 1e8 samples to X=3000 (memory-bounded, scripts/z52d_p2_SK0_avoid_chunked.py): ln δ/(ln X)^3 = −0.0246 (X=56), −0.0297 (178), −0.0281 (562), −0.0270 (1000), −0.0268 (3000). The local exponent of −ln δ in ln X over X=316–3000 is 2.7–2.9, so the exponent 3 persists within noise and shows no creep upward. The proposed X=10^4 is below the resolution floor (expected survivors ≈0.03 at 1e8 samples).

summary: Computed r3(n)=#{p+2^a+2^b+2^c=n} for odd n≤10^7 (C sieve; script SK0_sun3.c): mean r3/(ln n)^2 ≈ 1.12 at n≈10^7, slowly falling; a two-parameter fit over dyadic blocks gives ≈0.99(ln n)^2+1.9 ln n, consistent with the predicted log² intensity. Only odd n=3 has r3=0 in the range. For comparison p+2^a+2^b has mean ≈2.15 ln n (log¹) with no exceptions ≤10^7 except 3.

summary: Computed the Type II residue sets R(a,b) = {−e mod 4ab : e | a+b} for 1≤a≤b≤60: |R| = d(a+b) (all distinct), max |R| = 16, max |R|/(4ab) = 1/2. Sum-product bounds need |A| growing polynomially in the modulus, and here |A| ≤ 16 against moduli up to 14400, so no sum-product regime applies pointwise.

The independence test (observed survivor fraction vs the product of marginal hit-rates over the same families) was already done: data/z52b/dividing_indep_qnr.txt line 8 gives X=1000 observed=1.000e-04, independent=1.174e-10, ratio=852017.58; the decisive statement is in BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md item 3 (#329, l.44). This is the item's step, not a substitute.

scripts/z52d_p2_SK0_avoid_m.py runs the residue model with the general-m Type I/II families of Pomerance–Weingartner (Props 2.1, 2.3: moduli m·a·d and m·a·b); m=4 reproduces the repo's δ(1000)=1.2e-4. Survivor fraction at X=1000 (2·10^7 samples): m=5: 0 (<5·10^-8), m=6: 1·10^-7, m=7: 2.6·10^-6, m=8: 7.4·10^-3, m=12: 4.8·10^-2, m=15: 4.0·10^-3, so nontrivial survivors first appear at m=8, where PW Table 1 first lists nontrivial exceptions (m=5,6,7 only n=1,2). The model is not a perfect ordering (m=4 has survivors 1.2·10^-4 but no known exceptions), and the mod-840 sampling was chosen for m=4 only.
not_done: Only X≤3000 and one sampling scheme; the m=8..15 comparison is qualitative and not a fit.

summary: The OEIS b-files for A292624 and A192789 have only 1000 terms (primes up to 7919), not beyond 2·10^5. A292624 counts ordered triples: our check of the unordered reps (p=3: {1,4,12},{1,6,6},{2,2,3} → 6+3+3=12; p=5: 6+6=12) matches a(2)=12, a(3)=12. So the free extension premise is false, although our own prime range goes to 3·10^4 for the A3 count.
